narrative.origin_story: Sven Halvorsen runs investor relations and operations at a sixty-person climate-fintech in Oslo.
narrative.manifesto:
Remote work resolved distance. It did not resolve substance.

Today, distributed companies sign contracts over video, build squads in chat, present ventures in slides, run communities in feeds. It works. It does not feel substantial. There is no room. No territory. No persistent presence. Every interaction is a packet that arrives, is heard, and is forgotten.

We built Remotica to give substance back to distributed work — not by adding theater, but by adding architecture.

A decision room is a place. It has a calendar. It has minutes. It has the artifacts the decision was made over. It has the people who attended, recorded by name. Five years from now, when the company asks why a particular call was made on a particular Tuesday, the room is still there.

A venture territory is a place. The investor walks through the product, the roadmap, the team, the customer pipeline. They leave with attribution that is recorded — not "I was on a call once," but "I visited the venture territory on March 8th and saw the December roadmap."

An archive room is a place. The institutional memory of an endeavor lives there: every reviewed deliverable, every shipped milestone, every retro, every artifact. It survives departures. It compounds.

Remotica is what you reach for when the conference call is not enough — when a venture, a decision, or an endeavor needs to stop being a stream of packets and start being a place.
